region: Kigali — CND siege defense / Amahoro corridor
type: CND siege defense / urban rescue corridor
desc: Stationed at the CND Parliament under the Arusha Accords when the genocide began, Kayonga held the perimeter under sustained FAR assault with 600 soldiers. The battalion seized Mt. Rebero on April 11–12, using the high ground to shell FAR positions in the city center, and conducted mass rescue operations at Nyanza Hill. It held the Amahoro Stadium corridor until Kigali was fully liberated on July 4.
companies: Eagle Company — George Rwigamba — rescued ~5,000 people from Amahoro National Stadium
Chui Company — Rugambwa — contained advancing presidential guards
Tiger Company — Andrew Kagame — confronted Gendarmerie units
Simba Company — Aloys Gapfizi — repulsed military police units

points.label: Mt. Rebero captured — FAR positions shelled

region: Northern relief axis — Miyove · Rulindo · Kabuye → CND
type: Northern relief race — reinforcing CND siege
desc: Commanded by Col. Sam KAKA (KANYEMERA), deputy Lt. Col. Caesar KAYIZARI. Alpha raced south from Miyove through Rulindo and Kabuye to reinforce the besieged 3rd Battalion at the CND Parliament — holding that perimeter until Kigali's full liberation on July 4, 1994. Post-war, KAKA served as Army Chief of Staff, was elected to Parliament in 2003, and retired as Major-General. KAYIZARI later served as Army Chief of Staff (Land Forces), Rwanda's first Ambassador to Turkey (2013), and as FERWAFA president.

region: Kigali sweep west — Jali · Gisozi · Kacyiru · Gatonde · Ngororero → Gisenyi
type: Kigali urban assault then western drive to Gisenyi
desc: Commanded by Col. Ludovick TWAHIRWA ('Dodo'), deputy Lt. Col. John Peter BAGABO. Bravo fought through Kigali's eastern heights at Jali, pushed through Gisozi and Kacyiru, then swept west through Gatonde (Ngororero) and Ngororero town all the way to Gisenyi — cutting off FAR and Interahamwe escape routes to Zaire. Post-war, TWAHIRWA retired in 1998 to found Jali Investment Ltd and the Trinity transport company. Brig. Gen. BAGABO later served as Commissioner at the Rwanda Demobilization and Reintegration Commission, retiring from the RDF in August 2024.

region: Northeast sweep → Kigali → Ruhengeri — Muhambo · Ngarama · Kiramuruzi · Kayonza · Rwamagana · Kabuga · Kanombe · Rutongo · Jali · Shyorongi → Ruhengeri
type: Grand eastern arc — Uganda border to Ruhengeri
desc: Commanded by Col. William BAGIRE †, deputy Lt. Col. John MUGABO †. The 7th launched from Muhambo in the far northeast near Uganda, sweeping south through Ngarama, Kiramuruzi, Kayonza, and Rwamagana, entering the Kigali zone through Kabuga and Kanombe. After Kigali's liberation they continued north through Rutongo, Jali, and Shyorongi to reach Ruhengeri — one of the campaign's longest single-unit arcs. Col. BAGIRE passed away in January 1999. Lt. Col. MUGABO also fell in service. Both are remembered as heroes of the liberation.

points.label: Muhambo — 7th advance begins (NE Rwanda, Uganda border)

region: Southeastern Rwanda-only sweep — Mutara · Gabiro · Kayonza · Kibungo · Bugesera · Rwabusoro north bank · Nyanza · Ruhango · Kabgayi · Butare → Gikongoro
type: Southern grand sweep — NE Rwanda to Gikongoro
desc: Commanded by Lt. Col. Fred IBINGIRA (later Gen.), deputy Lt. Col. Eric MUROKORE. The 157th launched from Mutara in the northeast, swept south through Gabiro, Kayonza, and Kibungo, then stayed on Rwanda's side of the Rwabusoro north-bank corridor on May 25 before rescuing survivors at Kabgayi, liberating Butare on July 4, and pressing on to Gikongoro — covering Rwanda's entire southern corridor without routing through Burundi. Post-war, IBINGIRA served as Reserve Force Chief of Staff, was promoted to full General in 2018, and retired in 2023.

points.label: Rwabusoro north-bank corridor — inside Rwanda, May 25

region: North-central drive — Mukarange · Mugambazi · Rutongo · Butamwa · Gitarama → Ruhango
type: Central north-to-south thrust — Mukarange to Ruhango
desc: Commanded by Col. Charles K. MUHIRE, deputy Lt. Col. Douglas KAZINTWARI ('Gaddafi'). The 101st drove south from Mukarange through Mugambazi and Rutongo, pressed through Butamwa and seized Gitarama before completing the arc at Ruhango — tightening the central corridor. Post-war, MUHIRE served as Air Force Chief of Staff before retiring as Lieutenant General. Lt. Col. KAZINTWARI is frequently honored in historical accounts for his tactical precision.

region: Northern approach → Kigali — Rushaki · Rutare · Kanombe → Nyamirambo
desc: Commanded by Col. Charles MUSITU, deputy Lt. Col. Martin NZARAMBA. The 21st advanced from Rushaki through Rutare, swept down through Rutongo to Kanombe, and completed the liberation arc at Nyamirambo in Kigali — a critical final-phase objective that sealed the city from the west. MUSITU and NZARAMBA participated directly in the seizure of the Nyamirambo sector.

region: Northwestern axis — Birunga · Ruhengeri · Mukamira → Gisenyi
desc: Commanded by Col. Thadèe GASHUMBA, deputy Lt. Col. Alfred KAREBA †. Charlie Mobile Force advanced from the Birunga / Virunga volcanoes area through Ruhengeri town, swept west along the Ruhengeri–Gisenyi road through Mukamira, and completed the northwestern encirclement at Gisenyi — sealing the last major escape corridor before the DRC border. Lt. Col. KAREBA gave his life in service and is honored among the fallen heroes.

points.label: Birunga — Charlie advance begins (Virunga, NW Rwanda)

region: Kigali heights + western sweep — Kivuye · Rebero · Mt. Kigali · Butamwa · Gitarama → Kibuye
type: Kigali heights capture then western sweep to Kibuye
desc: Commanded by Col. Charles NGOGA † (deceased), deputy Lt. Col. Fred NYAMURANGWA. The 59th launched from Kivuye (Gakenke), captured the commanding heights at Mt. Rebero and Mount Kigali — enabling the RPA to observe and target government positions across southern Kigali — then pressed through Butamwa, Gitarama, and reached Kibuye. NYAMURANGWA is particularly remembered for the intense defense and capture of Mt. Rebero. NGOGA later served as Brigade Commander; he is deceased.
